items.title: Separate project document revisions from view counters and preserve atomic save conflicts
items.symptom: A GET followed by PUT with its returned expectedRevision can fail with PROJECT_REVISION_STALE even though the user did not edit elsewhere. Automatic saves also return 409 during simulation.

evidence.schema:
TABLE_NAME	COLUMN_NAME	COLUMN_TYPE	COLUMN_DEFAULT	EXTRA
projects	created_at	timestamp	CURRENT_TIMESTAMP	DEFAULT_GENERATED
projects	updated_at	timestamp	CURRENT_TIMESTAMP	DEFAULT_GENERATED on update CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
projects	view_count	int	0
evidence.nativeDragSaveReopen: Passed in both modes; the failure is not claimed to affect every save path.

items.rootCause: getProject reads an entity, then issues incrementViewCount. MySQL projects.updated_at is TIMESTAMP without fractional precision and has ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, so that counter write changes the persisted revision while the response maps the previously read entity. updateProject compares the supplied string directly with LocalDateTime.toString(). The existing read/compare/write sequence also needs a true atomic concurrency guard.
proposedWork: Introduce a migration-backed document revision independent of views/forks, or otherwise prevent counter updates from changing the edit token.
Make the revision comparison and document update atomic; preserve stale-write rejection for genuinely concurrent authors.
Normalize revision serialization and database precision; return the persisted revision in save acknowledgements.
Audit collaboration writes and autosave acknowledgements against the same revision contract.
acceptance: Two reads separated by more than one second increment views while returning the same document revision.
Immediate GET/edit/PUT succeeds against the real MySQL database; save/reopen retains components, wires, code and PCB data.
Two writers using one revision yield one successful edit and one 409 without lost updates.
No-change reads, simulation and view/fork counts do not make an editor dirty or invalidate a valid save.
Existing document/routing contracts plus real authenticated save/autosave tests pass.

resolution.documentRevision: Additive BIGINT column, exposed as a decimal string; independent of timestamp precision, view and fork counters.
resolution.concurrency: Originally SELECT FOR UPDATE; superseded by F008 version-checked UPDATE without an upload-time row lock. One success/one 409 and child rollback reverified against real MySQL.
resolution.counterUpdates: Explicit updatedAt self-assignment suppresses MySQL ON UPDATE for view/fork counters.
resolution.persistence: Remove unacknowledged delayed WebSocket writer. Authorized broadcasts remain; owner editor saves the whole document through guarded REST after two idle seconds or every ten seconds during continuous edits/retries.
resolution.client: Snapshots/settings send documentRevision; hydration compares numeric revisions and preserves the dirty editor baseline.
resolution.schema: Voltforge_BL/docs/schema/VFOPT_X_001_F001.sql applied to configured remote MySQL; project contents preserved. Other databases need the same one-time patch. Original Flyway history remains absent/disabled.
resolution.rollout: API rebuilt and restarted on port 2001. Reload previously open editor tabs. Existing user configuration changes preserved.

items.title: Align native WebSocket message limits and stop repeated reconnects for oversized canvas messages
items.symptom: The 36-component simulation repeatedly sends a canvas frame, loses Live Sync with close code 1009 and reconnects. This continues briefly after stopping simulation.

controlledProbe.reason: The decoded text message was too big for the output buffer and the endpoint does not support partial messages

items.rootCause: The native WebSocket decoder rejects frames smaller than the configured 1 MiB STOMP limit. Its close reason explicitly reports that the decoded text exceeds its output buffer and partial messages are unsupported. useCollaboration only blocks reconnect for a STOMP ERROR; close code 1009 schedules another connection, resets backoff after CONNECTED and replays pending dirty state. The source of the first dirty publication during simulation needs a revision trace.
proposedWork: Align servlet/native text-buffer limits with documented STOMP payload limits, or implement bounded chunk/delta transport with backpressure.
Treat a deterministic oversized-message close as an actionable failure instead of an automatic reconnect loop; retain the unsaved document.
Trace localDocumentRevision/isDirty changes when simulation starts and keep runtime-only updates out of the authored transport.
Verify transport limits across native WebSocket and any supported SockJS deployment.
acceptance: 4 KB, 12 KB and the measured 36.8 KB canvas payload succeed within the supported limit.
A deliberately over-limit payload produces one clear failure with no repeated reconnects or document loss.
A clean 60-second simulation has one stable collaborative connection and no repeated canvas publication.
Multi-user updates retain authorization, persistence and conflict handling after reconnect.

resolution.server: STOMP remains bounded at 1 MiB; servlet text/binary and outbound buffers are 2 MiB to allow SockJS wrapping. Authentication/origin/project guards remain enabled.
resolution.client: Complete UTF-8 frame size check, one actionable pause on STOMP ERROR or close 1002/1003/1007/1008/1009, preserved local edits, bounded transient retry with reset only after 30 seconds stable, disposal guards for old socket callbacks.
resolution.runtime: MotorLogic.onPinStateChange called authored updateNode during compiled AVR execution. All pin-driven writes in LogicRegistry and DigitalLogicChips now use updateRuntimeNode; live outputs still change without document/model revision changes.
resolution.persistence: Ordinary guarded autosave after reconnect passed. Over-limit local edits remain present and dirty when a separate REST save fails. Large-document persistence is explicitly open as F008.

attributeUpdateTrace2026_09_26.interpretation: An active MOTOR_DC (max_motor in the fixture) changes dashed-circle, opacity and shaft-rotation attributes repeatedly. The requests coalesce at the layer scheduler, but a changed animated attribute still invalidates the shared component layer.

items.title: Trace retained memory across repeated editor navigation
items.symptom: Post-GC JavaScript heap increases across all five editor/list cycles, although visible canvases, workers and collaborative sockets are released.

conditions.cycle: Open the actual editor; wait for actual Monaco; run compiled AVR for 1 second; navigate outside without manually stopping; wait 1 second; collect garbage; record resources. Repeat 20 times.

postWarmup.tolerance: At most 1 MiB and 5% after warmup; stable exited-editor DOM/listeners; zero models/workers/sockets/canvases/stages on every exit.

heapSnapshotDiagnosis.snapshots: Cycles 5 and 20; generated raw snapshots removed after analysis.
heapSnapshotDiagnosis.before: Added copies of geometry and wire-signature strings retained through nested runtime-action closures and previous simulation engines. Detached style and Text nodes grew by one each per visit through the Monaco global stylesheet Map.
heapSnapshotDiagnosis.after: No accumulating engine/geometry callback chain or new detached Monaco styles. The current canvas store still intentionally retains the latest document/route cache; three query entries remain stable. Most cycle-5-to-20 self-size growth is V8 compiled code/feedback rather than old editor instances.
heapSnapshotDiagnosis.intermediate: Restoring the runtime action removed the engine chain. Before the Monaco pin, two DOM nodes still accumulated per visit; after the pin DOM nodes stayed at 199 and listeners stayed at 218 after cycle 2.

limitations: Local AuthContext and API/STOMP fixtures; real production editor and compiled AVR; no authenticated backend coverage
Single fixed 36-node/75-wire project; this is bounded lifecycle acceptance, not a proof about unlimited distinct project/cache growth.

items.rootCause: SimulationEngine.runBatched temporarily replaced a Zustand action. An immutable write copied that closure to the latest snapshot, but cleanup restored only the captured older snapshot. The live action retained the engine and earlier editor scopes. The cached project query also captured the editor render scope. Separately, Monaco 0.55.1 removed disposed styles from the DOM without deleting them from its global stylesheet map. Navigation also left the global running flag true and allowed pending compilation/interpreter startup to finish after exit.
proposedWork: Capture heap snapshots after warmup and after at least 20 equivalent navigation cycles.
Identify dominators before changing cache ownership or adding cleanup.
Bound caches or dispose resources only where retention evidence supports the change.

items.symptom: A project PUT containing roughly 1.1 MB of Unicode canvas-property data returned HTTP 500 twice. The editor retained its local content as dirty, but the document was not saved. Initial cleanup DELETE also timed out waiting for a database lock.

items.rootCauseConfidence: TCP write reset and early lock confirmed; upstream reset origin not established
proposedWork: Trace request serialization, JDBC batching/driver, the remote MySQL network path and socket timeouts for large ASCII and Unicode documents.
Verify failed requests release transactions/locks promptly and cannot leave later reads, saves or deletes blocked.
Define a supported REST document budget and clear validation errors; avoid uncontrolled timeout increases or silent truncation.

items.rootCause: The deepest captured failure is SocketException: Connection reset by peer while Connector/J writes TLS packets. The subsequent batch/rollback errors mask it. SELECT FOR UPDATE already held the project row during upload. The server session allowed 28,800 seconds idle and 120-second lock waits, so a lost rollback could strand that lock. The same 1.1 MB request later succeeded unmodified; a fixed packet-size ceiling is not supported by the evidence.

resolution.concurrency: Use @Version on existing document_revision and check it in the actual UPDATE; remove early SELECT FOR UPDATE. Flush the changed parent for code-only/no-op saves, return the persisted version and translate competing updates to 409. Child updates roll back with a losing writer.
resolution.writes: DynamicUpdate avoids retransmitting unchanged JSON or overwriting separately incremented view/fork counters.
resolution.transport: Enable MySQL protocol compression within existing TLS. Driver connect timeout 5 s, socket read timeout 15 s, create/update/delete transaction timeout 20 s. No global database settings changed.
resolution.recovery: Session row-lock wait 5 s; abandoned idle transaction fallback 60 s, with existing 30 s pool keepalive. Normal failure rolls back immediately; network failure can still require the bounded server-side idle cleanup. Availability/timeout failures return structured 503.
resolution.budget: 4 MiB UTF-8 JSON per project POST/PUT, including escaping and metadata. Read at most limit+1 bytes before parsing/transactions, including chunked input. Structured 413 for oversized requests; nested code-file validation now applies (50 files, 1,000,000 characters/file).
resolution.editor: Check UTF-8 budget before upload. Keep local content and dirty state. Pause unchanged automatic retries after 400/409/413 or local size rejection; real edits and explicit Save can retry.
resolution.schema: No additional schema change; uses F001 document_revision column.

items.title: Prevent large single-line code edits from freezing the editor
items.symptom: A previous production test injected 920,003 characters through keyboard.insertText and froze the renderer. That was originally mislabeled as clipboard paste. Actual clipboard paste and model loading remain responsive. Follow-up production checks also exposed real keystrokes being lost immediately after switching files.

evidence.mode: Unmodified production bundle, real authenticated fixture
evidence.resultingWholeDocument: Above the 4 MiB save budget; UI must remain responsive enough to reject/reduce it.
evidence.cleanup: Terminated only the identified temporary production runner and its Chrome child processes; private fixture removed.
evidence.editor: Monaco via @monaco-editor/react; wordWrap on; native EditContext textbox in current Chrome
evidence.inputMethodCorrection: The original test used keyboard.insertText, not Ctrl+V. Its pasteCharacters field records the injected text length. Cumulative renderer CPU is a process snapshot, not a measured paste duration.

items.rootCauseConfidence: Synthetic typed-input stall reproduced with an external watchdog; native paste/model load measured separately; timed lost-edit guard reproduced and corrected.
proposedWork: Profile bounded large-file and long-line workloads without leaving hung test browsers running.
Keep model load, paste, wrapping and tokenization responsive within documented code-file limits; use size-aware editor settings or a safe large-file mode as evidence warrants.
Ensure oversized edits can be rejected or reduced with clear feedback before expensive rendering, with no silent truncation or lost local content.
acceptance: Representative large multiline code and long single-line code open and can be edited within a measured responsiveness budget.
A paste exceeding the supported save budget leaves the editor responsive and preserves recoverable content or clearly rejects the edit before applying it.
Normal syntax highlighting, typing, undo/redo, autosave and read-only behavior remain correct.
Verify with the production bundle and bound/clean up browser test processes.
items.rootCause: Monaco 0.55.1 handles keyboard-source type input one character at a time in CursorsController.type, whereas paste applies one TypeOperations.paste edit. Sending a 920,003-character typed event exercised that expensive path. Separately, CodeEditor ignored all onChange events for 100 ms after file/view switches, dropping real user input even though Monaco displayed it. The React Monaco wrapper already suppresses its own controlled value updates.

resolution.editor: Remove the timed ignoreChange guard. Keep explicit read-only/Full Sketch guards and rely on the existing Monaco React controlled-value suppression. Immediate edits now reach dirty state and persistence.
resolution.performance: No size-dependent wrapping/tokenization change is warranted by the measured clipboard/model-load path. Existing word wrapping, language highlighting and editor options remain enabled.
resolution.regression: Extend the existing editor browser runner with --code-editor. Native Ctrl+V plus onDidPaste assertions distinguish clipboard paste from typed input; tab/view transitions freeze time at 32 ms to catch the former 100 ms loss window. An external 8 second watchdog terminates only the owned browser if an editor action stalls.
resolution.cleanup: The reusable regression supports --no-artifacts and restores the prior clipboard. Temporary production/probe scripts, reports and test projects are removed after summarizing results.

validation.conditions: Installed headless Chrome, Monaco 0.55.1. Production: 1440x900, fresh uninstrumented dist build, real Keycloak/API and configured remote managed MySQL. Reusable regressions: 1366x768, Vite StrictMode with intercepted API.

responsivenessBudget.note: Scheduling proxy measured after clipboard preparation; not physical keyboard-to-pixel latency. Results are local workload observations, not universal device guarantees.
